item.title: tree-wide: Remove usage of AUR from packages marked as secure
item.description:
Rationale behind this PR is explained in the two commit messages.

I wasn't sure if the "security" label is appropriate since this is in the end more proactive caution then any active security risk as-is, feel free to remove it again.

tree-wide: mark packages using the AUR for src as insecure

urxvt-vtwheel and wemeet have sources directly fetched from the AUR. The AUR has been compromised numerous times over the last months and as such there is a high risk of malware accidentally being included with these packages on future updates. As such these have been marked as insecure.

With gtkimageview it is unclear if the sources also come from the AUR, it is not a normal package listed in the package repository, only a package in the AUR, yet its sources are fetched from sources.archlinux.org. Since its unclear, it has also been marked insecure.

tree-wide: vendor patches and small files fetched from the AUR

Since the AUR has been victim of numerous malware campaigns over the last couple of months and currently lacks procedures to prevent these attacks from happening again, all patches and small files currently fetched from the AUR are vendored with this commit.

All files are stored in the same format as their original fetchers would have stored them in the Nix store.

item.title: tengine: drop
item.description:
Proposing to drop tengine (i kinda fucked up my first PR #548595 so here's a new one :see_no_evil:).

Reasoning:

  • The current latest release is at this point over 3 years old and according to their own account they have at least 26 unresolved CVE in the current stable release: https://github.com/alibaba/tengine/issues/2050#issuecomment-5152263604
  • This should have been marked as vulnerable quite a while ago but unfortunately noone noticed it until now. It stands to reason that users of this package might also be unaware of the great risk they find themselves in.
  • They did publish a Release Candidate of a new version yesterday but since there have been multiple broadly reported nginx vulnerabilities this year and those still aren't addressed by a released stable version it stands to reason that the approach to security doesn't really reflect best practices.
  • There seems to be no plan to offer targeted security fixes (we have a stable branch which also needs to be considered).
  • Since the package is using the services.nginx options it shouldn't be to difficult for users of this package to switch to an alternative.

With all of this in mind to me the responsible thing seems to be to drop it. At least for now. If things improve it's still always possible to re-add it at a later point.

If this is merged i plan on opening a separate PR to mark it as vulnerable on 26.05.

item.title: angie: mark as vulnerable due to insufficient nixpkgs maintainer attention
item.description:
My impression is that currently angie doesn't recveive the attention within nixpkgs it actually should get if there are active users.

The only currently listed maintainer @Izorkin has has done some review work of angie in the not to distant past but it doesn't seem to be enough. I fully sympathize with not always having time for everything. So definitly no blame here. My intention with this PR is simply to protect the users of this package.

For example the latest (bot based) version bump was opened about 3 weeks ago. Since then another version was tagged which addreesses three CVEs:

  • #542017

Also in the past backports to the stable branch haven't really happened until i looked into it (but i'm actually not a user of that package so that isn't sustainable):

  • #526997

Given that it's an nginx fork and recent experiences with nginx vulnerabilities it kinda does seem irresponsible to offer an unpatched nginx fork without a warning to it's users.

So my proposal would be to add a knownVulnerabilities entry to it. If there is active maintainer interest and for example an additional maintainer keeping an eye on it this can easily be removed again. Otherwise the value proposition of an under maintained nginx fork within nixpkgs doesn't seem justified to me given the human (and monetary) costs attached to every single package.

I hope my reasoning for opening this PR is understandable.
